name: New York City
hook: Five boroughs, one skyline, and the canal that made it the capital of the world.

facts.label: the five boroughs
facts.statement: New York City is made up of five boroughs: Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Staten Island.

facts.label: the Empire State Building
facts.statement: The Empire State Building, designed by William Lamb, was inspired by a pencil standing point-up; Andy Warhol filmed its facade for eight hours.

facts.label: Central Park
facts.statement: Central Park opened in 1859 with Frederick Law Olmsted as chief designer; Christo and Jeanne-Claude's The Gates filled it with 7,503 orange gates in 2005.

facts.label: the Erie Canal
facts.statement: The Erie Canal opened in 1825, linking New York City to the Great Lakes and cutting freight rates from Buffalo from $100 to $10 a ton.

facts.label: Boss Tweed
facts.statement: Boss Tweed ran Tammany Hall's corrupt "Ring" and escaped from jail in 1875, fleeing to Cuba.

facts.label: Columbia University
facts.statement: Columbia University hosted Franz Boas's first U.S. anthropology department in 1902; Bennett Cerf and Herman Wouk both edited its humor magazine, Jester.

facts.label: the first U.S. capital
facts.statement: New York City was the first U.S. capital, where George Washington took the first presidential oath in 1789, and has been called "The Capital of the World."
